passage: In the waiting area of the bank branch, token number 42 was still glowing red, so Nikita took out a notebook. "Before we open the joint account, let's put everything on paper," she said. Nilesh turned to a blank page. Salaries first. Then Nikita's education loan payment and Nilesh's two-wheeler loan. Then the savings in a recurring deposit, and the plan to rent a bigger flat next year. As the page filled, Nilesh laughed softly. "I thought you had far more debt than this." "I thought the same about you," Nikita said. Their token was called. They walked to the counter like two people on the same team, who could finally reason with facts and not with guesses.

qa.a: They wrote down the plan to rent a bigger flat next year.

passage:
Dear Zubin,

You asked how Sadia and I are handling money after the wedding. Short answer: better than I expected, because of one evening.
Two weeks after we got back, she said, "Let's put everything on the table. All of it." I was nervous. I had my education loan EMI, which I'd only mentioned vaguely. She had her own loan, and a small savings account from her first job that I didn't know about.
We wrote it all on one sheet: both salaries, both EMIs, what we'd saved, and what we each wanted in five years. Hers: a small flat. Mine: finishing my loan early and one trip abroad.
Seeing it together changed the conversation. We stopped guessing about each other and started asking, "What can we do as a team?"
We're meeting a financial adviser next month to look at options together.

Irfan

qa.q: What did Irfan want in five years?
qa.a: Finishing the loan early and one trip abroad.

qa.q: How did Irfan feel when Sadia suggested putting everything on the table?
qa.a: Irfan felt nervous, having only mentioned the education loan vaguely before.

qa.q: What else could Irfan and Sadia do to keep working as a team?
qa.a: They could set a regular time to look at the sheet together, and use the adviser's input to choose options they both agree on.

qa.q: How might Sadia see the evening they laid everything out?
qa.a: Sadia likely felt relieved and closer to Irfan, since the guessing stopped and they could plan as one team.

passage:
Bidisha, you asked how Vivek and I stopped fighting about money in our first year. I'll tell you exactly what we did.
I'm Kashish, and I used to be the person who hid bank messages. Not because anything was wrong, just habit.
About three months after the wedding, we had a silly argument about a phone he bought. I realised we were each guessing about the other's money. So one Sunday I said, "Let's write everything down. Everything."
It took two hours. His salary, mine. His education loan EMI, which was bigger than I'd thought. My savings, which were smaller than he'd assumed. Then what we wanted: he wanted a car in two years, I wanted to do a master's.
Once it was all on one page, we weren't arguing about a phone anymore. We were two people looking at one plan.
Honestly, that page saved our first year.

qa.q: How long did it take Kashish and Vivek to write everything down?
Why did Kashish want to write everything down after the phone argument?
qa.a: Kashish felt uneasy that they were both guessing about each other's money, and wanted to replace suspicion with a shared, honest picture.

qa.q: What else could Kashish and Vivek do with the page?
qa.a: They could look at it together regularly and, for bigger goals like the car or the master's, talk to a qualified adviser about their options.

qa.q: How might Vivek have felt learning Kashish's savings were smaller than he assumed?
qa.a: Vivek may have been surprised, but seeing everything openly probably made him feel trusted and less anxious than guessing.
